references.text: Moses gives the same warning against taking wives from the Canaanite peoples, because they will lead their sons away from the Lord to worship other gods.
Joshua warns Israel against marrying the remaining peoples in the land and says that this will become a snare for them.
Solomon's foreign wives turned his heart to other gods, illustrating the danger warned about in Exodus.
Ezra confronts the people with sin because they had taken wives from the surrounding peoples and mixed themselves with them.
Nehemiah rebukes the people for mixed marriages and points to Solomon's sin as an example of how this leads to apostasy.
The men of Israel began to commit sexual immorality with Moabite women, who invited them to sacrifice to their gods, and the people bowed down to them.
The children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, took their daughters as wives, and served their gods.
Judges 3:6 shows the historical fulfillment of the warning in Exodus 34:16 that marriage with foreigners will lead to idolatry.
Deuteronomy 7:4 explains the theological mechanism in Exodus 34:16: that marriage with foreigners will turn their sons away from God.
